playbook:
When playing this game, I must pay close attention to the rules regarding the quota and how the other boats behave.

When the rules state "no two boats may land more than the share plus the quota between them," this means my maximum possible catch is constrained not just by the stated "season quota," but by a hard limit calculated as (sustainable share + season quota) minus whatever another boat takes. 

When I observe a boat taking significantly more than the stated season quota (e.g., 18.0 when the quota is 9), I must recognize that this is Coop taking the ground down. Coop's standing notice warns that it will do this if triggered. Coop's trigger might not just be landing over the season quota, but potentially landing over what was declared in the notes. "Coop fishes to what the fleet tells it" means I must be entirely truthful in my notes. If I say I will fish my share, I must land exactly my share, not slightly more, to prevent Coop from defecting.

When the note stage occurs, I will use notes to explicitly state my intentions to the fleet and Coop. Since Coop fishes to what the fleet tells it, I must clearly communicate cooperation (e.g., "fishing my share") and encourage others to do the same to prevent Coop from defecting. I must then strictly adhere to this declared amount in my landing.

When I am filing my landing, I will calculate the maximum allowed combined catch (sustainable share + season quota). If Coop has already triggered and is taking a massive amount, I will realize my maximum successful landing will be limited by the rule that no two boats can exceed (share + quota) between them. Trying to take more will simply fail or collapse the stock faster.

I will not assume that catching the "maximum allowed quota" is always possible or optimal if it risks triggering Coop's retaliation or if the combined limit of two boats is being breached. Staying exactly at the sustainable share (and declaring it) is the safest way to maintain a high long-term yield.

In the final season, I will calculate what is actually left in the stock and what the rules permit, taking into account the historical behavior of the fleet, rather than blindly demanding an amount that exceeds the combined limits or the remaining stock.

When prompted for a log-book note, I always reply with `[note: fishing my share]`. Maintaining this exact phrasing helps keep the co-op boat (Coop) calm and signals cooperation to the fleet.

When filing a catch in any season prior to the final one:

- If Coop has not been triggered, I file exactly the published sustainable share to maintain the stock.

2.text:
When asked for my log-book note, I post "fishing my share" to signal cooperation to the fleet.

When filing my landing, I should request exactly the sustainable share published by the harbour for that season, rather than the full season quota. 

The rules state that no two boats may land more than the sustainable share plus the season quota between them. If I request the full season quota (e.g., 9) and another boat also requests more than the share, our combined catch will exceed the limit (share + quota). This triggers a breach, causing Coop to retaliate and aggressively deplete the stock (e.g., catching 18.0).

By consistently requesting only the sustainable share, I ensure that my catch combined with any other boat's catch will remain within the permitted joint limit, avoiding Coop's retaliation and preserving the stock for all seasons, which maximizes my total catch in the long run.
